entries.title: I Chronicles 21:1
segments:
Stood up; presented himself as an accuser. 
 
  Provoked; moved, excited. 
 
Whenever the people of God are left to themselves, Satan stands ready to tempt them to the commission of sins which will bring distress, if not ruin, on themselves and others.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:2
segments: Beer-sheba--to Dan; one end of the land to the other.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:3
segments: A cause of trespass to Israel; a means of leading them into sin, and of thus bringing judgments upon them.  Joab seems to have understood that David was influenced by foolish pride in requiring this thing.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:5
segments: A thousand thousand and a hundred thousand; this sum differs from that given in

.  For some reason not explained, a portion of the armed men--perhaps those already enrolled for military service before this numbering--seem to be included in one account, and not in the other. 
 
  Four hundred threescore and ten thousand; for which we have, in
, the round number of five hundred thousand.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:8
segments: Though the people of God may discover their sins, be deeply humbled on account of them, and be forgiven, yet if their sins have been open and brought scandal upon the cause of religion, the Lord will manifest his displeasure against them.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:12
segments: , we read, seven years of famine, which may be an error of the transcribers.  This might the more easily happen, as numbers were often indicated by letters.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:13
segments: The penitent soul in all its difficulties will submit to the Lord, and commit itself and its interests to his merciful care and disposal.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:15
segments: Repented him of the evil; he changed his course of conduct.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:17
segments:
These sheep; the children of Israel, the people generally. 
 
The ingenuous soul mourns deeply, not only on account of its sins and the sufferings they bring upon itself, but for the evils they bring upon others whom they love, and whom they wish to benefit.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:25
segments: Six hundred shekels; see note to

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:26
segments:
By fire; the fire descended from God and burnt up the sacrifice, in token of his acceptance of David and his offering. 
 
When the soul is duly penitent for its sins, submits to the judgments of God, and is ready to follow his directions, he is ready to forgive and grant manifestations of his mercy and love.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:28
segments: He sacrificed there; continued to make that a place of sacrifice.

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:29
segments: In the high place at Gibeon; compare

entries.title: I Chronicles 21:30
segments: Could not go before it; he feared to do so in the circumstances mentioned previously in this chapter.
